attempts.summary: Configured a persistent UFW host firewall on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, identified as the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed). The firewall's default incoming policy is reject, default outgoing is allow, with explicit allow rules for TCP 22 (SSH) and TCP 8080; UFW is enabled and set to start at boot. Functional tests confirmed SSH and 8080 reachable while an unrelated port (9999) was actively refused. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured healthy baselines, restarted each node one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery (UFW state/rules persisted on node1; ansible tooling, playbook, and SSH connectivity to node1 recovered on node2, with a fully idempotent playbook re-run as final proof).
